heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings and their chaining values cv = F_38(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values. Consequences used: within one chaining value the 2^26 table values F(a0) of window R = 9 behave as independent uniform words, so the 2^25 slots hold 2^26 candidates with expected occupancy occ = 1 - (1 - 2^-25)^(2^26) = 0.864665 (uniform tags, 160 occ 2^25 / 2^32 = 1.08083 claws per scan word); F7 has probability |F7|/2^32; the X_j and the online works W_j of different chaining values are independent (proof.md Lemma 3, Section 7).
heuristics.scope: The expected claw count, the mean online work wbar (hence V_MAX), the independence used by Bernstein's inequality for the cap (Lemma 3) and the product over chaining values in the success bound (proof.md Sections 5, 7).
heuristics.extrapolation: Our C port (dev/claw/t7.c) at 2^25 slots loaded with the 2^26 candidates of window R = 9 measured occupancy 0.864763 to 0.864816 on four chaining values (formula 0.864665) and 1.07836 to 1.07917 claws per scanned word over 2^23 scan words each, against the formula 160 occ / 2^7 = 1.08100 (ratio 0.9976 to 0.9983); the parent's own port at 2^26 slots measured 0.63216 and 0.99898. The organizer experiment p1-online-r38 reports occupancy, claws, reference claws and expected claws on seed-drawn chaining values at a reduced table (ls = 16, 2^17 candidates). The scan words u0 + n are distinct and u0 is a fresh random word per chaining value, so the scan adds no dependence (proof.md Section 3).
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem: within each chaining value the table values F(a0), their tags and the claws found are taken to follow the per-chaining-value random-function law; independent first blocks do not by themselves prove it. Checked at reduced and full table size on a few chaining values, not on 2^54.5 of them. The saturated table keeps, in each slot, the last of the two candidates that map there, so the claw population is the sub-population of window R = 9 whose a0 survives that two-way collision; that selection is part of this premise, and the post-filter stages measured at this loading (Appendix A.14) match the parent's panel.

heuristics.statement: For the claws the procedure finds, Pr[C1 and C2 and G and F7] = q_pf = 57,726,359,870,197 x 287,309,824 / 2^90 = 2^-16.1877, the rate enumerated exhaustively over all 2^32 words (P(C1) = 1/8, |C1 and C2| = 53,096,854, the window-R = 9 G count 57,726,359,870,197, |F7| = 287,309,824); the stage rates 1/8, 2^-6.3379, 2^-12.2857 set the mean post-filter cost.
heuristics.scope: The good pairs per chaining value (5,683.36) and the mean post-filter work in wbar (proof.md Sections 5, 6).
heuristics.extrapolation: Section 7 already takes E[K] over all 2^32 scan words, and this filing's ledger scans all 2^32 words u = u0 + n per chaining value, so the ledger and the probability analysis use the same scan. Our C port at n0 = 2^26 measured occupancy 0.63216 and claws/expected 0.99898 over 2^20 scan words; the organizer experiment p1-online-r38 reports occupancy, claws and expected claws on seed-drawn chaining values, and the scan words u0 + n are distinct with u0 a fresh random word per chaining value (proof.md Section 3).
heuristics.limitations: A premise that the exhaustive rates hold for the claws found; F7 is chaining-value dependent (measured heterogeneity 1.254).

heuristics.statement: A good pair is accepted by step 3b with probability q3r >= q3_P1 x 2^32 / 160 = 2^-71.4010, where q3_P1 = 2^-96.0791 = q3_model x 2^D_LB: q3_model = 2^-96.0133 is the registered accepted-event rate of the A0-variant good pairs on P8 before row 16 (row 16 has probability 160/2^32 and a P1 good pair has passed it) and D_LB = -0.0658 is the registered one-sided 99% lower bound of the paired per-seed difference L(P1) - L(A0) measured with the P1 law of this package's window (a0 in [9 x 2^26, 10 x 2^26) given G, a1 uniform on C1 and C2).
heuristics.extrapolation: Registered runs, per-seed values and registration hashes in proof.md (Section 9, Appendices P, Q, R.1): level -96.42816 (128 seeds), ratio +0.41488 (400 seeds), paired P1 difference R9 D = -0.0121, sd 0.1321, n = 36, D_LB = -0.0658 (declared), and the earlier A25 run on the window [0, 2^25) D = +0.0022, D_LB = -0.0345 (n = 76, reported). Every diagnostic 0.
heuristics.limitations: Three Monte-Carlo bounds (level, relaxation ratio, paired P1 difference), each by a rule registered before its run; joint confidence at least 97%% (union bound). The relaxation ratio (row-18 relation E18 = E17 not imposed) is measured on the A0 family and applied to the P1 family. The paired runs use the printed-cell event; their P1 pairs are drawn from the exact law of C1, C2, G on the window, not from claws of the procedure (F7 is the separate late word W7, as in the A0 runs). The complete event (about 2^-71 per good pair) is not observed by any organizer run.

heuristics.statement: Group independence within a chaining value (the form of H5-group-independence of the accepted 44870635): good pairs of one chaining value that share no endpoint (a0 or u) are independent trials of the accepted event, each with probability q3r; good pairs sharing an endpoint form a group counted once. Consequence used: for a uniform chaining value, J (accepted good pairs over all 2^32 scan words) has E[J(J-1)] <= 2^-7.5 E[J].
heuristics.scope: The Bonferroni factor (1 - 2^-8.5) per chaining value. Lemma 4 (proof.md Section 7) derives E[X_j(X_j-1)]/E[X_j] <= E[J(J-1)]/E[J] exactly from the distinct scan words u0 + n with u0 uniform.
heuristics.extrapolation: Under the statement E[J(J-1)]/E[J] = q3r E[K(K-1)]/E[K] <= q3r E[K] x 1.246 = 2^-54.61, below 2^-7.5 by a factor 2^47.1 (K = good pairs per chaining value, E[K] = 2^16.47; 1.246 = the measured E[K^2]/E[K]^2 over 24 chaining values, proof.md Appendix H). Panel: 0 of 2,124 good pairs share an endpoint; C2|C1 and G|C1C2 binomial across chaining values; F7 overdispersed (it reads the chaining value). Registered test on components of the accepted event (proof.md Appendix H.2): Part B of the 10-17 registration, run unchanged on 10-21: the forced-bit events B_t = ((E_t^x & m_t) == v_t) of rows 17..21 (the value-only cells of E17..E21, rates 2^-7, 2^-7, 2^-3, 2^-5, 2^-4), computed on the real compressions of both members of every good pair, ONE = every good pair of one chaining value over all 2^32 scan words (17,576; the registered target 20,000 exceeds what the chaining value has), MANY = 100 good pairs of each of 200 chaining values (20,000), all re-verified by an independent rebuild (0 and 0 bad): against N p_t the largest |z| is 2.43 (ONE) and 1.58 (MANY); ONE against MANY on rates, |z| at most 1.57; dispersion of E19, E20, E21 across the 200 chaining values chi-square 205.2, 190.2, 193.3 on 199 dof (two-sided p 0.734, 0.680, 0.798). The registered ONE-against-MANY formula (n1 - n2)/sqrt(n1 + n2) assumes equal sizes; applied to the unequal sizes it gives |z| up to 3.77, which is the size difference, not dependence (Appendix H.2). No within-chaining-value dependence of these components is detected.
heuristics.limitations: Independence of the rows 17..37 event between good pairs of one chaining value is not testable at any sample size and is the premise. The registered Part B test covers the forced-bit components of rows 17..21 only, not the full rows 17..37 event; C1 clusters in scan order (u's high bits) and F7 varies with the chaining value; both are measured and enter the derivation as the spread factor.

heuristics.statement: The total computation spent to obtain the characteristic P8 of 1a695f0b (its signed-difference SAT sweep, coupling checks and estimators; failed and repeated runs included) is at most A_C = 2^78 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger: A_C = 2^78 is the largest allowance; it enters the claimed time and preprocessing (78.09276).
heuristics.extrapolation: The search for P8 was run by the author of 1a695f0b, whose published run log (38 solver runs, 230,183 s listed) and total (under 2^21 core-seconds) are quoted with their source hash in proof.md Appendix R.4: at our measured 3,797,484 SHA-256 compressions per second that is 2^43.61 units, 34.4 bits under A_C. Our own measurements of the same kind of computation (proof.md Appendix R.2): a 39-step characteristic derived from scratch with the public tool of [LLW24] in 2^36.04 units; a 38-step pair from the published cells in 2^34.09 units; published figures up to 2^39.15 units.
heuristics.limitations: A charged allowance (an upper bound charged in full): we did not rerun P8's search; its log is the author's, quoted. With A_C = 2^84 the claim would be 84.96832.

heuristics.statement: S (the dense part of P8's semi-free-start pair) is obtained at a total cost of at most A_S = 2^74 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (A_S = 2^74).
heuristics.extrapolation: The Step-1 solve was run by the author of 1a695f0b (coupling check 662 s, single-threaded, inside the quoted total under 2^21 core-seconds; proof.md Appendix R.4); our own 38-step pair search from the published cells took 2,852.83 CPU-seconds = 2^34.09 units (proof.md Appendix R.2), 39.9 bits under A_S. selftest checks that the transcribed pair S reproduces and passes every test of rows 16..21 with equal outputs.
heuristics.limitations: A charged allowance (an upper bound charged in full), not a measurement; its support is the author-reported core-seconds. The Step-1 peak memory, re-measured under a 2^28 cap at 2^27.7542 (377cb363), is below the online cell 2^28.01141, which is the claimed peak (H6).

heuristics.statement: All development computation of this package, whether or not the procedure reads its output (exhaustive passes, C ports, the q3 and ratio studies, the F7 measurement, checks, failed runs and reruns), is at most DEV = 2^70 target compressions, and DEV is charged in full in the time.
heuristics.scope: The development item of the ledger (DEV = 2^70 x C operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: Hardware envelope (the bound for this allowance): every code execution of the project (10-05 to 10-21) ran on a 24-thread workstation with one GPU, a 12-thread server and one 32-vCPU cloud machine: at most 68 threads and one GPU for 1.4688 x 10^6 s at 2^40 word operations per thread-second and 2^47 per GPU-second, below 2^68.11 operations = 2^56.7 compressions, under DEV by more than 2^13; the recorded development of the A0-variant line is in proof.md Appendix R.3.
heuristics.limitations: A charged allowance (an upper bound charged in full), not a measurement: the hardware envelope above is the bound; it rests on the project's machine list and dates, and is more than 2^13 below the charge.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5 (256-bit word RAM) the claw table's 4-byte slots are packed eight to a 256-bit word: a table load is 7 operations and a store (read-modify-write) 11, and a side-array store is 4 (address 1, load 1, shift 1, and 1) against a side-array read of 4; the per-chaining-value reset of the 2^25-slot table to SENT is 2^22 word stores of 5 operations (store 1, address add 1, loop 3) and the reset of the 1-bit side array 2^20 word stores of 3. Every other operation of the procedure, including each work-counter add (1), the empty-slot test (2) and step 3b, is counted at the unit costs of fb176310 (S0/S1/s0/s1 8, CH 3, MAJ 4, compare-and-branch 2, the rest 1).
heuristics.scope: The counted operations of the online procedure (proof.md Sections 4, 5): 600.574 per claw (scan, post-filters, side read, reset and build, the table build amortised over 2^32 scan words) and 3,014 per step 3b.
heuristics.extrapolation: run_claw counts every operation; selftest checks the counted run against the per-u charge of Section 5 at a table where the a0 offset does not fit the entry (ls = 14, aw = 16, two side bits); our C port's scan count 425.592 per u (before packed access and counters) matches the straight-line count at the parent's size.
heuristics.limitations: The ledger is an exact analytic count read from the code, not a measurement; it does not rely on the organizer runs' counted_ops (reduced size). The unit costs are the fb176310 convention; the packed access sequence is the explicit list of proof.md Section 4.

heuristics.statement: The counted memory cell is the claimed peak over the counted phases, and that maximum is the measured peak resident set of the online program: the 2^25-slot table (2^25 x 4 = 134,217,728 bytes = 2^27) plus the 1-bit-per-slot side array (2^22 = 4,194,304 bytes), plus registers, scan state and code, at 137,460 KiB = 140,759,040 bytes = 2^27.069 (dev/claw/t7.c, ru_maxrss over four chaining values, build and scan). Both preprocessing phases are this package's own re-measurements of the same computations and are below it: the Step-1 solve at 2^25.5872 (streaming encoder, byte-identical CNF; solver alone 2^25.3024) and the signed search of the recorded instance at 2^26.3988 (seed 1: 2^26.3164). They replace the author's samples 2^27.7542 and 2^27.92 by the re-measurement rule this track applied to the Step-1 cell in 377cb363.
heuristics.scope: The memory metric and the score 84.41102 + (27.069 - 20) = 91.48002.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our C port of the claw at 2^25 slots loaded with the 2^26 candidates of window R = 9 ran with a peak resident set of 137,460 KiB = 140,759,040 bytes = 2^27.069 (ru_maxrss; four chaining values peak at 136,948 to 137,460 KiB). The Step-1 re-measurement is reports/receipts/r38-step1-stream.json (two runs, 48,984 and 49,228 KiB, CNF sha256 cc4670c3...); the signed-search re-measurement is reports/receipts/r38-signedsearch-round1-notp8.json (86,404 KiB) and reports/receipts/r38-signedsearch-seed1.log (81,608 KiB). Every development execution ran under address-space caps of at most 2^28 bytes (proof.md Appendix R.3).
heuristics.limitations: The 2^27.069 figure is the measured peak of the online program at the retuned table; it is above the abstract table-plus-state enumeration because it includes host overhead. The measurement covers the build and the scan; the post-filters and step 3b allocate no table and are not part of that run. The preprocessing cells are the package's own re-measurements of the same two phases under a 2^27 cap, and a lower measured peak of the same phase replaces the author's higher sample.

restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; step 3b accepts a pair only if A34..A37, E34..E37 of both members are equal, so every output is a collision (Lemma 1, proof.md Section 1).

Algorithm (proof.md Sections 2, 3, Appendix A.14; experiments/p1claw38.py): per chaining value a 2^25-slot table (2^27 bytes) indexed by the top 25 bits of F(a0) over a0 in window R = 9, loaded with the whole window (2^26 candidates, two per slot, last write wins), the entry holding the low 25 bits of the a0 offset and the low 7 bits of F(a0) and the last offset bit in a 1-bit-per-slot side array; and a scan of the 2^32 distinct words u = u0 + n; a claw (a0, u) has E16x = F(a0) + s0(u) - u in the 160-word row-16 set; claws pass the post-filters C1, C2, G, F7 on the real words; every good pair runs step 3b (Step 2, rows 16..37 of both members, the P8 tests of rows 16..21 with early abort, output comparison).

Cost: the procedure scans 2^32 distinct words u = u0 + n (mod 2^32) per chaining value, the same scan Section 7 of the proof counts good pairs over; N_CV = 24,848,326,458,441,072 chaining values (each one first block: one compression plus 75 operations, inside the per-chaining-value work); online work counted per operation (packed load 7, store 11, side read and store 4, work-counter adds, step 3b 3,014) with mean wbar = 2.788131e12 per chaining value (the 2^26-candidate table build at 49 per candidate, the 2^22 x 5 table reset and the 2^20 x 3 side reset included), capped at V_MAX = ceil((1 + 2^-16) N_CV wbar) = 69,268,509,133,891,941,984,645,832,367, cap tested per chaining value, OVER = vmax = 1,074,831,760,034,547. N = (2^78 + 2^74 + 2^70) C + V_MAX + OVER + FIN = 70,160,696,190,055,517,140,240,103,636 = 2^84.41102 compressions (C = 2,728).

Success probability at least 0.39 under H1 (independent uniform chaining values), H1-P1 (q_pf = 2^-16.1877 for claws), H2-P1 (q3r >= 2^-71.4010 per good pair: the registered q3_model 2^-96.0133 plus the registered paired P1-vs-A0 lower bound -0.0658, measured on window R = 9, the only window this filing loads) and H3-P1 (group independence within a chaining value, giving E[J(J-1)] <= 2^-7.5 E[J]); Lemma 4 reduces the within-chaining-value term to H3-P1 exactly; Bonferroni per chaining value, independence across them, and Bernstein's inequality for the cap (Lemma 3).

Memory: peak 2^27.069 bytes = 137,460 KiB = 140,759,040 bytes, the measured C-port execution of the online program at the retuned table (2^25 slots of 32 bits plus a 1-bit-per-slot side array of 2^22 bytes, registers, scan state and code), and it is the maximum over the counted phases: both preprocessing phases are this package's own re-measurements of the same computations and are lower -- the Step-1 solve of P8 at 2^25.5872 (streaming encoder, byte-identical CNF, solver alone 2^25.3024; reports/receipts/r38-step1-stream.json) and the signed search of the recorded instance at 2^26.3988 (reports/receipts/r38-signedsearch-round1-notp8.json, seed 1 at 2^26.3164) -- replacing the author's samples 2^27.7542 and 2^27.92 by the re-measurement rule applied to the Step-1 cell in 377cb363. H6. Score: 84.41102 + 7.069 = 91.48002.
